assignmentHtml.task:
研究 Apache Druid 用于支持交易平台分析平台的架构。具体调查：

  1. 数据摄取——Kafka 超集查询、批处理、流处理、实时处理。
  2. 更新与删除——历史数据段替换、深层存储、墓碑。
  3. 连接——受限的连接，以及在查询时与 MySQL/PostgreSQL 进行连接。
  4. 多租户隔离——角色、权限、容量规划。
  5. 恢复——控制器与高可用性、ZooKeeper/Zookeeper-lite，以及恢复操作会恢复哪些内容。
  6. 许可证——Apache 2.0。
  7. 版本注意事项。
    重点关注 Druid 在迟到事件、CDC 风格更新和多表一致性方面能够做什么、不能做什么。
assignmentHtml.context: 证据截止日期为 2026-09-16。针对开源分析平台的设计调研。工作负载包括通过 Kafka 传入的每天 3TB 点击流、通过 CDC 处理的可变订单、Iceberg 数据湖连接、多租户报表、擦除与恢复。仅考虑开源版本。不要假定主分支的行为。
assignmentHtml.expected_output: 为 Apache Druid 提供结构化调研档案章节，涵盖架构、数据摄取、更新与删除、连接、隔离、恢复、许可证、版本注意事项，并附来源 URL。

answerHtml: Apache Druid architecture dossier covering ingestion (Kafka streaming with exactly-once, late-event capability, Superset via pydruid/SQLAlchemy), updates/deletes (immutable segments; time-range REPLACE/overwrite; tombstones from zero-row MSQ; soft-delete then kill-task; deep storage retains data indefinitely unless auto-kill enabled), joins (native broadcast hash-join restricted to Druid datasources; MSQ broadcast/sort-merge; lookups via JDBC extension for key-value dims only — NO built-in JDBC joins to MySQL/PostgreSQL at query time), multi-tenant isolation (datasource-per-tenant or tenant_id dim; RBAC via authenticator/escalator/authorizer; tiered Historicals, query priority, dedicated Brokers), recovery (Coordinator/Overlord leader election via ZooKeeper or Kubernetes extension; deep storage as permanent backup; export-metadata tool restores 5 metadata tables but not segment files themselves; kill tasks irreversible), license (Apache 2.0), and version caveats (ZK segment loading removed in 30.x; Hadoop ingestion removed 37.x; Java 11 dropped 35.x; SQL null/bool semantics changed 28.x; no literal 'ZooKeeper-lite' feature — K8s extension provides ZK-free mode).

evidence.snippet: Druid has Master (Coordinator + Overlord), Query (Broker + Router), and Data (Historical + Middle Manager/Peon/Indexer) servers. External dependencies: deep storage (S3/HDFS), metadata storage (MySQL/PostgreSQL/Derby), ZooKeeper for service discovery, coordination, leader election.
evidence.supports: Full component inventory and external dependency map for architecture section

evidence.snippet: Segment lifecycle: indexing → deep storage push → metadata publish. Appending uses single version per time chunk; overwriting creates new version with atomic replacement. Exactly-once via transactional offset+metadata commit. Broker ensures consistent segment versions per query. Default HTTP-based segment discovery since 25.0.0.
evidence.supports: Atomic replacement, MVCC-style segment versions, exactly-once guarantees, late-event handling via timestampSpec and offset commits

evidence.snippet: Window period restriction removed — Kafka indexing service can ingest data with arbitrarily old timestamps. If event stream contains wide timestamp range relative to segment granularity, results in many small segments; periodic compaction recommended.
evidence.supports: Late events are supported in streaming; trade-off is segment proliferation, not data loss

evidence.snippet: Concurrent append and replace (experimental): new append lock (sharable) and replace lock (exclusive) allow streaming ingestion to append late data while compaction replaces segments on same interval without conflict.
evidence.supports: Version caveat + mechanism enabling late-event appends alongside compaction

evidence.snippet: Soft delete: mark segment 'unused' (metadata-only, fast). Hard delete: kill task permanently removes from metadata store and deep storage; irreversible. Auto-kill via Coordinator duties, default off, 90-day retention when enabled. Reindexing with filter for specific record deletion.
evidence.supports: Two-phase delete model; kill task is destructive; tombstones implied via 'unused' state

evidence.snippet: MSQ ETL producing zero rows publishes empty tombstone segments that overshadow valid data. Recovery: mark newer tombstone UNUSED then older segment USED (Druid always prefers newest version). Only recoverable if segments exist in deep storage and aren't auto-killed. Tested on 34.0.0.
evidence.supports: Tombstone behavior explicit; restore procedure; deep-storage dependence

evidence.snippet: Druid stores data in immutable segments. Updates via REPLACE OVERWRITE ALL / WHERE (time-range based), or partial overshadowing (smaller granularity segment on top of larger). Compaction needed to fix fragmentation. Does not support single-record updates by primary key.
evidence.supports: No PK-based updates; time-range replacement; overshadowing for row-level-ish updates

evidence.snippet: Native join datasource: broadcast hash-join; INNER/LEFT only; right-side inputs must fit in memory; condition must be equality. SQL accepts any condition but inefficient ones degrade to cross-join + filter. No predicate pushdown past joins. RIGHT/FULL OUTER partially implemented/unreliable in native engine.
evidence.supports: Join limitations: memory-bound broadcast, no FULL OUTER reliability, no predicate pushdown

evidence.snippet: MSQ joins: broadcast (default, LEFT/INNER/CROSS, 30% processor-memory limit on broadcast tables) or sortMerge (all join types incl. FULL, 10MB per-key buffer limit). Both require equality conditions if present.
evidence.supports: MSQ join algorithms and limits; sort-merge enables large joins at cost of performance

evidence.snippet: Lookups: in-memory key-value mappings replacing dimension values. Do not have history — always current. JDBC supported via lookups-cached-global extension. Updated via Coordinator config propagation to query-serving processes.
evidence.supports: JDBC lookup extension exists for MySQL/PostgreSQL key-value dims; NOT full relational joins; no temporal history in lookups

evidence.snippet: Multitenancy: separate datasource per tenant (independent schema/partitioning/rules, faster queries, wasteful JVM/segments) vs shared datasource with tenant_id dim (partition by tenant via multi-dim range partitioning or Kafka hash). Historical tiers for hot/cold data distribution. Query priority flags; dedicated Brokers per tier; Router for routing.
evidence.supports: Tenant isolation patterns and capacity planning mechanisms

evidence.snippet: Security model: Authenticator (basic/LDAP/Kerberos) + Escalator (inter-process auth) + Authorizer (RBAC). Roles assigned to users; permissions on resources (DATASOURCE/STATE/CONFIG) with READ/WRITE actions; resource names treated as regex patterns.
evidence.supports: RBAC framework enabling per-datasource access control for multi-tenant isolation

evidence.snippet: HA requires: ZooKeeper cluster of 3-5 nodes; replicated MySQL/PostgreSQL metadata store; multiple Coordinators/Overlords with automatic failover (one active, others redirect); Brokers scaled out behind load balancer.
evidence.supports: HA topology and failure modes for coordinator/overlord/broker

evidence.snippet: Kubernetes extension enables Druid without ZooKeeper: druid.zk.service.enabled=false, druid.serverview.type=http, druid.discovery.type=k8s. Service discovery via pod labels/annotations/readiness; leader election via K8s ConfigMaps. Experimental; all pods in same namespace with RBAC for pods/configmaps.
evidence.supports: ZK-free operation is possible via K8s extension — the functional equivalent of 'ZooKeeper-lite'; marked experimental

evidence.snippet: Export-metadata tool exports 5 metadata tables: segments, rules, config, datasource, supervisors. Only Derby export currently supported. CSVs reimportable to Derby/MySQL/PostgreSQL. Can rewrite deep storage paths. Tool does NOT copy segment data files — deep storage contents must be migrated separately.
evidence.supports: What a restore restores: metadata records only; deep storage files are separate responsibility

evidence.snippet: Segments marked unused remain in deep storage with metadata intact; recoverable via 'Mark as Used all segments' after fixing load rules. Coordinator kill task disabled by default; when enabled, default retention 90 days before deletion.
evidence.supports: Default configuration favors recoverability; what must be preserved for restore

evidence.snippet: Apache Druid and documentation licensed under Apache License 2.0. Uses Hadoop, Kafka, MySQL, ZooKeeper; embeds Curator, Jackson, Jetty, Joda Time, Ning Compress.
evidence.supports: License is Apache 2.0; third-party components listed

evidence.snippet: ZK-based segment loading removed in 30.0.0, disabled in 31.0.0. Hadoop ingestion removed 37.0.0 (deprecated 34.x). Java 11 removed 35.0.0, Java 8 removed 32.0.0. MSQ core since 35.0.0. SQL null/strict-booleans changed 28.0.0 (feature-flag revertible). Front-coding v1 default 26.0.0. Segment metadata cache on by default 37.0.0. Rolling upgrades unsupported from <0.23.
evidence.supports: Critical version caveats across recent releases; no feature named 'ZooKeeper-lite' exists — ZK dependency reduced via HTTP defaults and K8s extension

evidence.snippet: Superset connects to Druid via SQLAlchemy with pydruid package. Connection string: druid://{user}:{pass}@{host}:{port}/druid/v2/sql (default port 9088). Native Druid connector ships behind DRUID_IS_ACTIVE flag but pydruid preferred.
evidence.supports: How Superset queries Druid: standard SQL endpoint /druid/v2/sql

evidence.snippet: ZooKeeper used for: Coordinator leader election, Historical segment publishing protocol, Overlord leader election, Overlord/MiddleManager task management. Druid continues serving queries using last known good state during ZK outage.
evidence.supports: ZK's role and graceful degradation behavior
